title: Mixed-trophies biofilm cultivation in capillary reactors
author: Heuschkel, Hoschek, et al.

steps.title: Obtain microbial strains
steps.instruction: Acquire Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 from the Pasteur Culture Collection (PCC, Paris, France) and Pseudomonas taiwanensis VLB120 from the in‑house collection or DSMZ (reference 26739.1).

steps.title: Prepare Synechocystis pre‑culture
steps.instruction: In a 100 mL baffled shake flask with cotton plug add 20 mL YBG11 medium (no citrate) and inoculate with 200 µL cryo‑stock; incubate at 30 °C, 150 rpm (2.5 cm amplitude), 50 µE m⁻² s⁻¹ LED, ambient CO₂ (0.04 %), 75 % humidity for 4 days.

steps.title: Grow Synechocystis main culture
steps.instruction: Transfer pre‑culture to fresh 20 mL YBG11 medium in a 100 mL baffled shake flask, adjust to OD₇₅₀ = 0.08, and incubate under the same conditions for 3 days.

steps.title: Prepare Pseudomonas pre‑culture I
steps.instruction: In a 20 mL test tube add 5 mL LB medium, inoculate with a loopful of P. taiwanensis VLB120 cryo‑stock, and shake at 30 °C, 200 rpm (2.5 cm amplitude) overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Pseudomonas pre‑culture II
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL M9 medium (5 g L⁻¹ citrate, US* trace elements) to a 100 mL baffled shake flask, inoculate with 200 µL of pre‑culture I, and incubate at 30 °C, 200 rpm for 24 h.

steps.title: Grow Pseudomonas main culture
steps.instruction: In a 100 mL baffled shake flask add 20 mL M9 medium (5 g L⁻¹ citrate, US* trace elements), inoculate from pre‑culture II to OD₄₅₀ = 0.2, and incubate at 30 °C, 200 rpm for 8 h.

steps.title: Prepare mixed‑species suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Synechocystis and Pseudomonas main cultures at 5000 g, room temperature, 7 min; resuspend each pellet in 2 mL YBG11 (no citrate, 50 mM NaHCO₃). Mix the two suspensions and inoculate 20 mL fresh YBG11 (no citrate, 50 mM NaHCO₃) to OD₇₅₀ = 1 (Synechocystis) and OD₄₅₀ = 1 (Pseudomonas); incubate in a 100 mL baffled shake flask for 24 h at the Synechocystis conditions.

steps.title: Prepare feed and waste bottles
steps.instruction: Use two 2 L bottles (one feed, one waste). Fit each with a GL45 3‑port cap and a GL14 cap equipped with a pressure‑compensation set and sterile 0.2 µm filter. Assemble the GL14 cap with its insert, attach PTFE tube mb.1 so its end lies ~1.5 cm above the cap, and tighten. Connect mb.2 to the lower end of mb.1 and to a straight tube connector (ISM 694); the opposite end of this connector will later link to tubing a.1. Assemble the waste bottle analogously with tubing wb.1 and wb.2. Open the GL14 screw caps slightly before autoclaving and wrap bottle tops in aluminium foil.

steps.title: Autoclave tubing and connectors
steps.instruction: Wrap all Tygon tubing (a.1‑a.7, b.1, b.2) and all connectors in aluminium foil; autoclave dry and straight (limit 8‑10 Tygon pieces per run).

steps.title: Assemble capillary reactor tubing
steps.instruction: Under a clean bench, connect a.1 to the medium bottle via straight connector mb.2, then to pump tube a.2. Connect a.2 to a.3, and a.3 to the injection port using Luer‑lock connectors. Attach the opposite end of the injection line to a.4, then a.4 to a T‑connector. Connect b.1 (sterile filter) to the T‑connector and b.2 to the same T‑connector; keep the airline clamped for single‑phase operation. Cut a sterile 1 mL pipette to 20 cm, attach it to the T‑connector as a capillary (a.5), then connect the capillary to a.6 and via straight connector to a.7. Finally, link a.7 to the waste bottle through straight connector wb.2.

steps.title: Condition reactor with medium flow
steps.instruction: Run medium through the assembled reactor at 52 µL min⁻¹ for 2 h to equilibrate the system.

steps.title: Inoculate capillary reactor
steps.instruction: Stop the flow, clamp the inlet of the injection port, and inject 2 mL of the mixed‑species cell suspension (designated 1 ci) into the system. Keep the reactor closed.

steps.title: Allow cell attachment in dark
steps.instruction: Leave the reactor without flow for 24 h, keeping the capillary unit in darkness to prevent photosynthetic O₂ evolution.

steps.title: Restart flow and set illumination
steps.instruction: Re‑open the inlet tubing, resume medium flow at 52 µL min⁻¹, and turn on the light source above the capillary at 50 µE m⁻² s⁻¹ (measured at the unit).

steps.title: Switch to segmented air‑liquid flow
steps.instruction: When the culture turns yellow (≈11 days, indicating O₂ stress), open the airline and introduce air segments at the same rate as the medium (52 µL min⁻¹) to lower dissolved O₂. Continue cultivation; biofilm can be grown for up to 34 days.

steps.title: Measure dissolved oxygen
steps.instruction: Polarize the Clark‑type OX‑500 microsensor, calibrate per manufacturer, and connect the flow cell (filled with medium, bubble‑free) to the inlet or outlet of the capillary. Record current in mV and convert to µmol L⁻¹. After measurement, rinse the flow cell sequentially with 96 % ethanol, 0.01 M HCl, and water (alternatives: 0.1 M NaOH or isopropanol). Store the sensor tip exposed to water or air; it may remain polarized for up to 5 days.

steps.title: Measure gas‑phase oxygen
steps.instruction: Autoclave custom bubble traps, connect to inlet or outlet, ensure tight silicon sealing. Equilibrate the trap in segmented flow for 24 h. Flush a Hamilton gas‑tight syringe 1–2 times, withdraw 100 µL gas, inject into a gas chromatograph for O₂ analysis. Clean the syringe with water followed by acetone after use.
